title: 20. Gateway API & Cilium eBPF Networking
summary: Master the next-generation Kubernetes Gateway API spec (Gateway, HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute) and Cilium eBPF L7 kernel-level network security policies.
prerequisites: eBPF fundamentals and Linux socket filtering
learningObjectives: Design and deploy Kubernetes Gateway API Gateway and HTTPRoute resources for canary traffic splitting
Configure fine-grained weight-based traffic routing without external service mesh proxies
Author and enforce Cilium L7 HTTP-aware CiliumNetworkPolicy resources in the Linux kernel
Troubleshoot Gateway listener attachment and HTTPRoute parent binding status

curriculumModules.title: Kubernetes Gateway API: Role-Oriented Ingress Architecture
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Gateway API splits ingress into GatewayClass (Infra Provider), Gateway (Cluster Operator), and HTTPRoute (Application Developer), providing expressive canary splitting, header matching, and multi-namespace routing.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Shared enterprise Edge Gateway with delegated HTTPRoute objects across product development namespaces.

curriculumModules.title: Cilium eBPF CNI & Layer 7 Kernel Security Policies
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Cilium leverages eBPF programs loaded directly into the Linux socket layer, enforcing Layer 7 HTTP path and method restrictions without iptables or userspace Envoy proxy overhead.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Zero-trust kernel-enforced CiliumNetworkPolicy blocking unapproved HTTP verbs (e.g. enforcing GET only on public endpoints).

labs.title: Gateway API Weighted Canary Traffic Splitting
labs.scenario: Your product team is releasing a new checkout service version. Configure a Kubernetes Gateway API HTTPRoute that splits ingress traffic 80% to checkout-v1 and 20% to checkout-v2 canary.
labs.productionContext: Gateway API HTTPRoute rules provide standardized weight-based canary deployments across cloud providers without proprietary ingress annotations.
objectives: Deploy the core Gateway resource edge-gateway listening on port 80
Deploy the HTTPRoute checkout-route with 80% weight to checkout-v1 and 20% to checkout-v2
Validate route attachment to parent Gateway
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: edge-gateway
  namespace: production
spec:
  gatewayClassName: cilium
  listeners:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      protocol: HTTP
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: checkout-route
  namespace: production
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - name: edge-gateway
  rules:
    - backendRefs:
        - name: checkout-v1
          port: 80
          weight: 80
        - name: checkout-v2
          port: 80
          weight: 20

steps.title: Review Gateway and HTTPRoute Definitions
steps.instruction: Open the Manifest Editor and inspect the edge-gateway and checkout-route manifests.

steps.title: Apply Gateway API Resources
steps.instruction: Deploy the Gateway and HTTPRoute to the production namespace.

steps.title: Verify HTTPRoute Traffic Weights
steps.instruction: Check that the HTTPRoute has the 80/20 weights configured.

validationRules.description: Gateway edge-gateway exists in production namespace with cilium GatewayClass
validationRules.name: edge-gateway
validationRules.remediation: Apply the Gateway manifest with gatewayClassName: cilium in production.

validationRules.description: HTTPRoute checkout-route exists in production namespace
validationRules.name: checkout-route
validationRules.remediation: Apply the HTTPRoute manifest in production namespace.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure namespace is explicitly set to 'production' on both the Gateway and HTTPRoute resources.

labs.title: Cilium L7 HTTP-Aware eBPF Security Policy Enforcement
labs.scenario: A security audit requires restricting frontend-to-backend traffic so that only HTTP GET requests on /api/v1/products are permitted, dropping all other methods in the kernel via eBPF.
labs.productionContext: Traditional NetworkPolicies only filter IP:Port (Layer 4). CiliumNetworkPolicy filters HTTP methods, paths, and headers (Layer 7) with sub-millisecond eBPF performance.
objectives: Allow ingress traffic to pods labeled app: catalog
Enforce Layer 7 rule permitting only GET requests on /api/v1/.*
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: secure-backend-l7
  namespace: production
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: catalog
  ingress:
    - fromEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            tier: frontend
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "80"
              protocol: TCP
          rules:
            http:
              - method: "GET"
                path: "/api/v1/.*"

steps.title: Inspect Cilium Network Policy Manifest
steps.instruction: Open the Manifest Editor and review the CiliumNetworkPolicy specification.

steps.title: Deploy Cilium L7 Policy
steps.instruction: Apply the secure-backend-l7 policy to the production namespace.

validationRules.description: CiliumNetworkPolicy secure-backend-l7 exists in production namespace
validationRules.name: secure-backend-l7
validationRules.remediation: Apply the starter manifest to create CiliumNetworkPolicy secure-backend-l7 in production.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Confirm that the port in toPorts is specified as a string '80' and the protocol is TCP.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which Gateway API resource is responsible for defining how client HTTP requests match and route to backend services?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: HTTPRoute is the standardized Gateway API resource created by application developers to route HTTP traffic.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does Cilium enforce Layer 7 HTTP filtering compared to standard Kubernetes NetworkPolicies?
options: By modifying host iptables rules only
By using Linux eBPF programs attached to the kernel socket layer for line-rate L7 parsing
By routing all cluster traffic through a central external load balancer
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Cilium uses kernel-level eBPF programs to inspect Layer 7 HTTP headers and paths with near-zero latency.
